summary: Pike State Forest lookout in Pike County, Ohio: 1934 construction and a planned occupant per newspaper items, NHLR registration in 2014, standing per the FLO list.

events.note: Land acquisition for Pike State Forest begins; restoration work with CCC and Division of Forestry help follows in the 1930s
Construction described as well underway in January 1934; completion date not confirmed
October 1934 item says the tower would be occupied by Ralph Newman of Latham; actual service not confirmed
Registered September 3, 2014, as US 1023, OH 12; nominated by Mark

evidence.supports: location in Pike State Forest, Pike County, Ohio
evidence.quote: Pike State Forest Pike County, Ohio
Date Registered September 3, 2014 Nominated by Mark

evidence.supports: 1924 start of land acquisition and restoration aim
evidence.quote: In 1924 the acquisition for the lands of the forest began, with the objective of restoring damaged woodland affected by fire and human interference

evidence.supports: 1930s CCC and Division of Forestry restoration work
evidence.quote: In the 1930s the Civilian Conservation Corps and the Division of Forestry undertook much of the restoration work.

evidence.supports: January 1934 construction well underway, just north of Latham; purpose to locate fires in southwestern Ross County
evidence.quote: The construction of another tower is well underway on Green Ridge, just north of Latham, Pike county. This tower will be able no doubt to locate fires in southwestern Ross county

evidence.supports: October 1934 planned occupant, Ralph Newman of Latham
evidence.quote: The new Green Ridge Tower one mile north of Latham in Pike county will be occupied by Ralph Newman of Latham.

evidence.supports: standing status and NHLR number in the FLO Ohio list
evidence.quote: Green Ridge Pike 39.11643 -83.23846 Tower Standing NHLR US 1023, OH 12

notes_for_editor: Thin record: the NHLR entry (no description), two 1934 newspaper items relayed by the Forest Lookouts site from the Chillicothe Gazette, and the Pike State Forest article. No design, height, completion date, staffing history or access found. Brief elevation 385.6 m agrees with NHLR 386 m. Suggest ODNR Division of Forestry or the Pike County historical society for build records. Access left unknown on purpose; no access level is supported.
